causal_boundary.not_supported: This is not an exact fixed-candidate receiver-side accept/reject ablation. Dynamic compilation changes which memory is delivered and how; trajectories can diverge. Do not attribute the full Full-vs-AMMI delta solely to a single compatibility predicate.
causal_boundary.supported: State-conditioned, step-wise memory delivery with legal abstention is strongly associated with substantially better ScienceWorld performance than static injection of the same memory bank, and Brief State contributes materially.

observations.claim: Runtime applicability is explicitly defined in terms of current subgoal relevance and whether a memory entry's assumed environmental conditions currently hold.
The compiler acts at each step and includes NOACTION=empty as a first-class outcome when no memory entry reaches sufficient utility.
On ScienceWorld/Qwen-2.5-14B, Full MemCompiler reports 46.67/69.33; w/o Brief State reports 38.50/60.67; AMMI static injection with the same memory reports 27.93/52.68; No Memory reports 31.11/45.26.

protocol_implication: Corroborates PER_DECISION_MEMORY_COMPATIBILITY_GATE and the legal empty-injection control: memory presence/retrieval is not durable authority to inject guidance.

source.title: MemCompiler: Compile, Don't Inject -- State-Conditioned Memory for Embodied Agents

tested_scope.memory_bank_control: The paper states the bank is deliberately minimal raw successful trajectories plus rationale; AMMI uses the same retrieved memory bank as static upfront context to isolate dynamic compilation.
